target.title: [AI-assisted] fix(cli): surface session lane busy exits
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #54622.

A same-session `openclaw agent` CLI dispatch can sit behind an active session lane and fail without telling the operator why. The command queue already has lane-wait diagnostics, but the Gateway/CLI path did not surface them as a structured result. This PR makes CLI-triggered lane waits return a deterministic `LANE_WAIT_EXCEEDED` result instead of a silent generic failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix keeps the queue ordering model intact and makes the CLI path opt in to terminal busy rejection when it is waiting behind an active same-session lane. It adds typed wait details, a `rejectOnWait` queue hook, an `AgentSessionLaneBusyError` helper, Gateway payload propagation, Swift/protocol model fields, CLI text/JSON rendering, and tests across queue, Gateway, CLI relay, and embedded-runner lane handling.

This refresh also preserves current-main queue timeout cleanup behavior: `taskTimeoutAbortSignal`, `taskTimeoutAbortGraceMs`, `taskTimeoutReleaseSignal`, and matching `QueueEntry` wiring remain carried through so timed-out embedded runs do not keep lanes held longer than intended. Non-CLI gateway agent calls are not opted into the busy rejection.

## User Impact

Operators now get a clear session-lane busy message and retry suggestion when a second CLI dispatch targets a session lane that is already busy. JSON-mode callers receive structured `errorCode: "LANE_WAIT_EXCEEDED"` details. Non-CLI agent runs and normal successful CLI runs keep the existing behavior.

No new dependencies, config, credentials, network surfaces, or queue policy changes are introduced.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof already supplied in this PR before the conflict refresh used a real Gateway service process and two source-entrypoint CLI `agent` processes against a mock provider. It showed:

- before: a second same-session CLI request eventually reached the provider and returned `SECOND_DONE` with no busy stderr;
- after: a second same-session CLI request exited non-zero before a second provider request and printed `Error: session lane busy (...)` plus a retry suggestion;
- long-active proof after the timer fix: the second request returned `LANE_WAIT_EXCEEDED` while active work was still occupying the lane.

Refresh proof on a local OpenClawUbuntu PR lane after resolving current-main conflicts:

- `git diff --cached --check`: PASS
- `oxfmt --check` on changed TypeScript files: PASS
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/process/command-queue.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts`: PASS, 3 shards in 88.75s; Gateway 380 tests, queue 35 tests, CLI relay 69 tests
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/lanes.test.ts`: PASS, 6 tests
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json ...`: PASS, 0 warnings, 0 errors
- `pnpm check:test-types`: PASS

Remaining proof gap: the live two-CLI runtime service proof was not rerun after this conflict refresh. The focused queue/Gateway/CLI/embedded-runner tests directly cover the repaired code paths, and the previous real Gateway/CLI behavior proof remains the real behavior evidence for the user-visible lane-busy output.
